papers.title: GROMTools: scalable individual-level GReX imputation for mega-biobank-scale cohorts
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The computational burden of individual-level genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) imputation has risen sharply with the growth of human mega-biobanks and the rapid expansion of transcriptomic imputation models across tissues and single-cell hierarchies. Existing tools were not designed for this setting and require complex, memory-intensive workflows that are poorly matched to shared and cloud-based compute environments, where runtime, memory, and I/O directly determine cost and throughput. GROMTools is an open-source C ++ engine with an R interface that exploits sparse prediction weights, streams PLINK2 genotypes, and writes compact binary outputs for scalable individual-level GReX imputation. Results In UK Biobank (UKB), benchmarks on chromosome 1 across 50,000-450,000 individuals, 388,017 variants, and 11,724 gene-model pairs from 32 single-nucleus transcriptome imputation models, GROMTools produced near-identical predictions to PrediXcan and PLINK2, with minimum Pearson correlation >0.999 and maximum RMSE <0.001 across all of the imputed genes, while reducing CPU time by about 100-fold and peak memory by about 33-fold. These gains make routine biobank-scale individual-level GReX imputation practical and cost-efficient on standard CPU infrastructure. Availability GROMTools is freely available at https://github.com/voloudakislab/gromtools under the GPL v3 license. Documentation is available at https://voloudakislab.github.io/gromtools/ .All scripts used for data quality control and benchmarking, together with log files and a snapshot of the GROMTools code version used for all of our analyses, are archived at DOI: https://zenodo.org/records/21926165

all_papers.title: GROMTools: scalable individual-level GReX imputation for mega-biobank-scale cohorts
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The computational burden of individual-level genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) imputation has risen sharply with the growth of human mega-biobanks and the rapid expansion of transcriptomic imputation models across tissues and single-cell hierarchies. Existing tools were not designed for this setting and require complex, memory-intensive workflows that are poorly matched to shared and cloud-based compute environments, where runtime, memory, and I/O directly determine cost and throughput. GROMTools is an open-source C ++ engine with an R interface that exploits sparse prediction weights, streams PLINK2 genotypes, and writes compact binary outputs for scalable individual-level GReX imputation. Results In UK Biobank (UKB), benchmarks on chromosome 1 across 50,000-450,000 individuals, 388,017 variants, and 11,724 gene-model pairs from 32 single-nucleus transcriptome imputation models, GROMTools produced near-identical predictions to PrediXcan and PLINK2, with minimum Pearson correlation >0.999 and maximum RMSE <0.001 across all of the imputed genes, while reducing CPU time by about 100-fold and peak memory by about 33-fold. These gains make routine biobank-scale individual-level GReX imputation practical and cost-efficient on standard CPU infrastructure. Availability GROMTools is freely available at https://github.com/voloudakislab/gromtools under the GPL v3 license. Documentation is available at https://voloudakislab.github.io/gromtools/ .All scripts used for data quality control and benchmarking, together with log files and a snapshot of the GROMTools code version used for all of our analyses, are archived at DOI: https://zenodo.org/records/21926165
all_papers.llm_title_zh: GROMTools：针对大型生物库规模队列的可扩展个人级 GReX 插补
all_papers.llm_title_bilingual: GROMTools：针对大型生物库规模队列的可扩展个人级 GReX 插补 / GROMTools: scalable individual-level GReX imputation for mega-biobank-scale cohorts
all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 随着人类大型生物库的增长以及跨组织和单细胞层次的转录组插补模型的快速扩展，个体水平遗传调节基因表达（GReX）插补的计算负担急剧增加。
llm_highlights_zh: 现有工具并非针对此设置而设计，并且需要复杂的内存密集型工作流程，这些工作流程与共享和基于云的计算环境不太匹配，在这些环境中，运行时、内存和 I/O 直接决定成本和吞吐量。
GROMTools 是一个带有 R 接口的开源 C ++ 引擎，它利用稀疏预测权重、流式传输 PLINK2 基因型，并为可扩展的个体级 GReX 插补编写紧凑的二进制输出。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: The computational burden of individual-level genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) imputation has risen sharply with the growth of human mega-biobanks and the rapid expansion of transcriptomic imputation models across tissues and single-cell hierarchies. Existing tools were not designed for this setting and require complex, memory-intensive workflows that are poorly matched to shared and cloud-based compute environments, where runtime, memory, and I/O directly determine cost and throughput. GROMTools is an open-source C ++ engine with an R interface that exploits sparse prediction weights, streams PLINK2 genotypes, and writes compact binary outputs for scalable individual-level GReX imputation. Results In UK Biobank (UKB), benchmarks on chromosome 1 across 50,000-450,000 individuals, 388,017 variants, and 11,724 gene-model pairs from 32 single-nucleus transcriptome imputation models, GROMTools produced near-identical predictions to PrediXcan and PLINK2, with minimum Pearson correlation >0.999 and maximum RMSE <0.001 across all of the imputed genes, while reducing CPU time by about 100-fold and peak memory by about 33-fold. These gains make routine biobank-scale individual-level GReX imputation practical and cost-efficient on standard CPU infrastructure.
